summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun
details: The package advertises itself as a small PostCSS selector-scoping plugin (index.js ~40 LOC implementing a `:where(...)` transform), but its npm `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])` to execute a bundled 727 KB `math_init.js`. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated: `setup.mjs` uses identifier-mangled imports (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and per-function string-lookup dictionaries; `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled module (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a rotated string-array VM (`WV8StW` shift routine) over thousands of packed constants, hiding its runtime behavior from static inspection. The alternate-runtime dispatch pattern (fetching a fresh interpreter to run the payload out-of-band from Node) is a Node-instrumentation evasion technique. The payload's function is unrelated to any legitimate need of a PostCSS plugin, which has no requirement for the Bun runtime or a large opaque module.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
